legal basis: Delaware General Corporation Law, Title 8, Subchapter XV (§361-§368): https://delcode.delaware.gov/title8/c001/sc15/
jurisdiction: Delaware, United States (form copied by other US states)
real examples: Allbirds PBC; Lemonade, Inc. (Delaware PBCs discussed in study)
measured outcomes where published (with: Empirical sample of 295 Delaware PBCs (2013-2019) raised >$2.5B; funded by traditional VC; average rounds somewhat smaller than peers. Source: https://openscholarship.wustl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1721&context=law_scholarship
known failure or controversy: Purpose-washing concern noted: strongest funding concentration in consumer-facing sectors where mission signaling may double as branding. Source: https://openscholarship.wustl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1721&context=law_scholarship

legal basis: Private certification and trademark run by B Lab (not a statutory corporate form): https://www.bcorporation.net/en-us/certification-notice
real examples: Nespresso Global; Danone North America; Patagonia Works
measured outcomes where published (with: Difference-in-differences studies report positive turnover/sales growth after certification; one study finds no significant short-run employee growth effect. Sources: https://doi.org/10.3390/su13137191 ; https://www.mdpi.com/2071-1050/12/20/8459
known failure or controversy: Criticism that multinational certifications can enable greenwashing/purpose-washing (e.g., Nespresso controversy raised by other B Corps). Sources: https://fairworldproject.org/news/press-releases/the-b-corp-standard-is-at-risk-fair-world-project-and-certified-b-corp-brands-call-on-b-lab-global-to-strengthen-standards/ ; https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ceq7lqley32o

mechanism: OpenAI mission-governed hybrid (nonprofit control over for-profit subsidiary, then PBC recap)
legal basis: OpenAI LP announcement (2019) plus OpenAI structure update (2025): https://openai.com/index/openai-lp/ ; https://openai.com/our-structure/
real examples: OpenAI LP (capped-profit era); OpenAI Group PBC controlled by OpenAI Foundation board rights
measured outcomes where published (with: During Nov 2023 governance crisis, Reuters reported more than 700 OpenAI employees threatened to quit and join Microsoft. Source: https://www.reuters.com/technology/openai-execs-invite-altman-brockman-headquarters-sunday-the-information-2023-11-19/
known failure or controversy: Board removed CEO Sam Altman citing candor concerns, then reversal and leadership reinstatement after internal revolt. Source: https://www.reuters.com/technology/openai-ceo-sam-altman-step-down-2023-11-17/

legal basis: Anthropic LTBT announcement (Class T stock; Delaware purpose trust): https://www.anthropic.com/news/the-long-term-benefit-trust
real examples: Anthropic PBC with LTBT trustee governance rights
known failure or controversy: Trust details are partly non-public; publicly discussed 'failsafe' allows sufficiently large stockholder supermajorities to amend trust powers, creating debate about enforceability. Source: https://corpgov.law.harvard.edu/2023/10/28/anthropic-long-term-benefit-trust/

legal basis: Country corporate/foundation law plus firm charters/articles (e.g., Bosch, Novo Nordisk Foundation, Carlsberg Foundation governance pages)
real examples: Robert Bosch GmbH (Bosch Stiftung share capital majority); Novo Nordisk A/S (controlled via Novo Holdings/Foundation); Carlsberg A/S (Carlsberg Foundation voting control)
measured outcomes where published (with: Danish evidence: lower leverage and higher survival; mixed return profile by size; large foundation-owned firms in one study show higher ROA (about 5.0% vs 3.6% for large non-foundation firms). Sources: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/corg.12236 ; http://www.tifp.dk/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/The-Performance-of-Danish-Foundation-Owned-Companies.pdf
known failure or controversy: Same Danish study reports slower growth and small-firm underperformance, highlighting governance trade-offs. Source: http://www.tifp.dk/wp-content/uploads/2014/04/The-Performance-of-Danish-Foundation-Owned-Companies.pdf

mechanism: Steward-ownership via trust control + mission-locked economics
legal basis: Private trust/nonprofit structure (Patagonia Purpose Trust + Holdfast Collective ownership design): https://www.patagoniaworks.com/press/2022/9/14/patagonias-next-chapter-earth-is-now-our-only-shareholder
real examples: Patagonia (2% voting stock to Purpose Trust; 98% non-voting stock to Holdfast Collective)
measured outcomes where published (with: Patagonia projected roughly $100M/year in dividends (when not reinvested) to Holdfast Collective. Source: https://www.patagoniaworks.com/press/2022/9/14/patagonias-next-chapter-earth-is-now-our-only-shareholder
known failure or controversy: Criticism focused on tax and political-finance implications of using a 501(c)(4) for the non-voting equity leg. Sources: https://archive.ph/OyzyZ ; https://fortune.com/2022/09/16/patagonia-founder-legal-tax-loophole/

legal basis: Spanish/Basque cooperative law plus Mondragon cooperative bylaws (one-worker governance within member co-ops)
measured outcomes where published (with: Reported 2025 results: €11.322B sales, 71,415 workers, +1,346 jobs. Source: https://www.tulankide.com/en/mondragon-achieved-a-turnover-of-eur11-322-billion-and-created-1-346-new-jobs-in-2025
known failure or controversy: Fagor Electrodomésticos bankruptcy (2013) raised governance and strategic-risk debates inside the cooperative model. Source: https://doi.org/10.1177/0143831X19899474

legal basis: Mitbestimmungsgesetz (Co-determination Act), 4 May 1976, generally for firms with >2,000 employees: https://www.worker-participation.eu/sites/default/files/2024-10/DE-%20MitbestG%20-%20%28amended%29%20-%20en.pdf
real examples: Large German corporations subject to parity codetermination rules (e.g., qualifying AG/GmbH/cooperatives)
measured outcomes where published (with: Quasi-experimental evidence finds no clear wage/rent-sharing effect but higher capital formation and higher value-added per worker (about +16% to +21%). Source: https://doi.org/10.1093/qje/qjaa038
known failure or controversy: Other studies report possible shareholder-value trade-offs and distributional shifts toward labor. Source: https://doi.org/10.2308/jiar-2022-055

mechanism: AI windfall clause / AI dividend redistribution proposals
legal basis: Windfall Clause proposal (Oxford/FHI/GovAI): https://cdn.governance.ai/Windfall-Clause-Report.pdf ; AI Dividend proposal example: https://www.alexbores.nyc/files/Bores-Dividend_Policy.pdf
real examples: Windfall Clause (O'Keefe et al.); AI Dividend proposal (Bores)
known failure or controversy: Not yet enacted as binding law in major AI jurisdictions; open concerns include enforceability, international coordination, and competitiveness effects (discussed in proposal papers). Source: https://cdn.governance.ai/Windfall-Clause-Report.pdf
